name: PT Bakrie & Brothers Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bakrie & Brothers: a book-value discount, a pledged CCT loan and a konglo premium
frontmatter.summary: BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed vehicle: a toll road to 2061, an uncovered EV sibling at book, and steel and digital businesses worth less than book. The primary mark is a book-value discount, not a sum of independent parts. The fundamental value is below the price; only the konglo lens carries the target. We keep HOLD, with no fundamental cushion.
thesis: The primary mark is not a sum of independent parts: CCT and VKTR are carried at book and the residual is parent equity less those two marks, so the total is book equity by construction. We relabel it a book-value discount and stop claiming the marks are the constraint.

The P/BV cross-check is rebuilt on premium-free peers. The previous set imported the DSSA and CUAN konglo premia; on ADRO, ASII and ABMM the leg is struck near book, and the fundamental value falls accordingly.

A house concession DCF of the toll road does not support its acquisition mark: at a market cost of capital the present value of the road's cash flow does not cover the project debt, so the mark is generous rather than conservative.

Governance is the discount's DNA and the record is fuller than the last draft said: a documented share pledge secures the Bank Nobu CCT-acquisition loan, most of the cash sits at the same bank, and a large stock of short-term investments and advances sits in offshore structures.

HOLD is a lens call, not a fundamental one: the twelve-month fundamental value is below the price, and the target is above it only because the konglo lens keeps part of the premium. The expected return is positive but thin.

catalysts.event: Maturity of the twelve-month Bank Nobu term loan that finances the CCT acquisition and is secured by the BNBR share pledge
The 2026 toll tariff adjustment on the Cimanggis-Cibitung section
Full-year 2026 results, the first audited read on post-rights interest cover and on the Nobu facility
Annual shareholders' meeting and any decision on the accumulated-loss position and a dividend
Regime - MSCI's decision on moving Indonesia to Standalone status

blocks.text: **What changed.** This revision accepts the red team's central point. The primary "sum of the parts" was not a sum of independent marks: CCT and VKTR are carried at book and the residual is parent equity less those two marks, so the total equals book equity by construction and per-share value is the holdco discount applied to book. Re-marking either part only moves the residual. We relabel the method a **book-value discount**, correct the P/BV leg to premium-free peers, and re-open the rating. The fundamental value is **Rp25** and the target **Rp42**. The rating stays **HOLD** because the konglo lens, not the fundamental, carries the target: the price is **Rp41**, the expected total return **1.5%**, and the fundamental value is below the price with no margin of safety.

**The call.** HOLD at **Rp42**, with a twelve-month fundamental value of **Rp25** below today's price; the target is above it only because the lens keeps **30%** of the log premium. That is a flow call on a thin float, not a view that the parts are worth the price.

Three things set the file. The value is one asset: the toll road, at net assets of **4,101** after the non-controlling-interest portion, with the project syndicated loan of **9,715** inside it [S12]. The nine months ran at a parent loss of **-342** because interest and financial charges of **815** exceeded operating profit of **596** [S29]. The balance sheet is opaque: short-term investments are **1,218**, advances for investment **901**, and **750** of the **954** cash balance sits at Bank Nobu, the lender that holds the pledge [S29].

What moves the value is the tariff schedule and traffic, the floating rate, and whether the manufacturing, EV and digital businesses ever earn their cost of capital [S12, S29]. The house concession DCF says the toll-road equity is worth less than its acquisition mark, so the bull is VKTR re-marked to the price a standby buyer paid, plus a tariff step; the bear is the same road with the discount at the top of its band and the pledged share overhang.

BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed industrial and infrastructure vehicle. It reports three segments - infrastructure and manufacturing, fabrication and construction services, and trading, services and investment - and its largest business by FY2025 revenue was the steel, pipe and construction group PT Bakrie Metal Industries at **2,200**, alongside the electric-vehicle group VKTR at **1,080** and smaller infrastructure and digital arms [S2, S12].

The asset that matters is the toll road. PT Cimanggis Cibitung Tollways operates the section between the Cimanggis and Cibitung junctions as the final link of the outer ring network, with a concession to 10 August 2061; traffic in the eight months to August 2026 averaged **43,911** vehicles a day on **2,500** of revenue a day, above the company's own budget [S15, S18]. The group took its ownership from a minority to full control on 28 November 2025, buying out PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur and PT Waskita Toll Road and taking over their shareholder loans [S12, S18]. The subsidiary note shows **100.0%** legal ownership through Bakrie Toll Indonesia, while the acquisition accounting carries a non-controlling-interest portion that implies a lower effective share; the filing does not reconcile the two, and we use the filed mark rather than gross up [S12, F44].

The rest of the group is smaller and thinner than its revenue suggests: steel and pipe into oil, gas and infrastructure; automotive components; EV buses; and early-stage solar and construction-printing ventures [S2, S15]. None carries a separately disclosed segment profit, which is why the residual is a book figure rather than a bottom-up mark.

Control is family-based and indirect. The stated controlling shareholders are Aburizal, Nirwan Dermawan and Indra Usmansjah Bakrie, through a chain of vehicles; the largest registered holder is an offshore company at **26.0%** and the public holding below five per cent each is **30.0%** at 31 December 2025 [S11].

The sectors are not one industry, and the house treats BNBR as a conglomerate. The macro regime tilts away from Indonesian rate-sensitive domestic demand, the wrong side for a group whose largest business is a domestic toll concession and whose balance sheet is floating-rate [S0].

The toll road is where the industry question lives. It is a regulated concession rather than a competitive business: the regulator sets the tariff and the term, and value comes from traffic growth over a period long enough that early debt service does not determine the outcome. Cimanggis-Cibitung is the final section of the outer ring, connecting the Soekarno-Hatta corridor to the Tanjung Priok hinterland, and it competes with the Jakarta inner ring and the Jakarta-Cikampek corridor [S22]. It is a genuinely good asset in a dense catchment, and its traffic is above both its internal budget and the company's comparison set [S15]. The concession is the scarce resource: the toll segment is closed to new entry and has no substitute in its corridor, so the operator's economics are set by the tariff schedule and the traffic ramp rather than by competition. The risk is regulatory - the timing of a tariff adjustment is a policy decision - and financial, because the concession is levered.

The rest of the group is a challenger in industries where it has no pricing power: steel pipe and fabrication into oil, gas and infrastructure; automotive components into domestic purchasing power; electric vehicles dependent on public procurement and local-content rules [S2, S15]. Steel and fabrication are cyclical and import-exposed, the EV business is a policy creature, and neither has covered its cost of capital through the cycle [S12, S15].

Regulation and policy therefore dominate: toll tariffs are set by the regulator, the EV business depends on procurement and local-content rules, and infrastructure contracts are awarded by the state [S15]. The rupiah and the floating-rate environment matter because the project debt is floating-rate, which the company singled out when it explained the nine-month loss [S26, S29].

On a five-forces reading, the toll road has negligible new-entry threat and no substitute in its corridor, which is why it is the only part worth close to its carrying value; the manufacturing, components and EV businesses face import competition, fragmented customers and modest switching costs, and their returns reflect that [S12, S15]. The moat is the concession document, and it belongs to one subsidiary.

**The nine months.** Revenue of **4,126** in the nine months exceeds the whole of FY2025 (**3,743**), on gross profit of **1,132**, operating profit of **596** and company-reported EBITDA of **810** [S29, S26]. The parent nevertheless lost **-342**: operating profit plus a **5** disposal gain less a **2** FX loss, **815** of interest and **70** of other charges gives a pre-tax loss, and the **48** net tax charge and the **9** non-controlling-interest credit take it to the parent loss [S29]. The tax is booked at profitable subsidiaries even though the group is in loss, so the engine would remove it; we carry it as a non-operating charge in FY2026E to reproduce the filed nine months.

**Debt and interest.** The rights issue cut gross debt to **2,054** of short-term and **11,275** of long-term loans at 30 September, against cash of **954** [S29]. The forecast runs the debt on that post-rights basis from FY2027E: FY2026E interest is struck on the opening balance because the issue closed in the third quarter, but the forward bill falls to about **903** [S29, S0]. Operating profit of **884** then covers interest about once in FY2027E and above once from FY2028E, rather than never - the red team's F5 correction. The forecast cash line is negative because the engine has no equity-issuance line; use the filed cash, not the modelled line.

**D&A and EBITDA convention.** The data pack is wrong on D&A: the audited FY2025 charge is **171** [S12], while the pack carries only the general-and-administrative allocation. The company's reported EBITDA of **810** is operating profit plus a depreciation add-back that excludes the **329** amortisation of the toll-road concession charged to cost of revenues [S29]. The model follows the company's convention; if the concession amortisation is added back too, EBITDA is higher and leverage lower.

Our forecast holds FY2026E revenue at the nine-month run-rate plus the third quarter again [S29, S26]. The gross margin is held at the nine-month **27.4%** and operating expenses at **13.0%** of revenue, the filed ratios, not the lower FY2025 ratios struck without the toll road [S29, S12]. FY2026E EBITDA is **1,112**, a **19.6%** margin; the step from FY2025 is scope, not margin expansion. The parent loss is **-376**, close to the nine-month actual [S0].

**Cash conversion and accruals.** The nine-month accruals ratio is (net income less operating cash flow) over average total assets: net income of **-342** against operating cash flow of **80** on total assets of **25,541** and **23,568** is negative, so earnings are not outrunning cash; it is not a manipulation flag [S29].

Capital allocation has run one way: towards the family's other vehicles and towards issuing shares. The 2024 quasi-reorganization removed **19,530** of accumulated deficit [S11, S12], and the July 2026 issue raised **4,714** and **263,337**m shares, most passed through to repay the BTI facility [S29, S19]. No dividend has been paid in the period covered by the price history [S6]. The IDX board and notation status is not directly stated in the archive; BNBR is not among the names the exchange removed from the special-monitoring board on 28 September 2026, and we report the absence of a special-board finding [S30, S0].

The house method for a conglomerate is to value it on its parts. That method cannot be applied as written here, and the red team's F1 is right to call it fatal. CCT is at book, VKTR is at book, and the "all other businesses" line is consolidated parent equity of **3,853** less those two marks: **4,101** and **262** [S12]. The three lines sum to book equity by construction; the bridge (rights proceeds of **4,714** less the nine-month loss of **-342**) takes the total to filed parent equity, and per-share value is the holdco discount applied to book. Re-marking CCT or VKTR only moves the residual, so we relabel the method a **book-value discount**.

We tested the two ways out. A bottom-up mark of the other businesses cannot be sourced: the archive has their revenue but no segment EBITDA or EBIT, so the residual stays at book with a zero-floor as a sensitivity. A house concession DCF of CCT can be built: revenue of **846**, EBITDA of **694**, operating cash flow of **684**, a run-rate of **2,500** of revenue a day, a concession to 2061 [S22, S15, F17], a net concession right of **15,019** over the remaining life and project debt of **9,715** [S29, S12]. At a market cost of capital the present value of the road's cash flow does not cover the debt, so the equity value is at or below zero. The acquisition mark of **4,101** is therefore generous, not conservative, and the bull does not claim a higher CCT mark. We keep the audited acquisition value as the base because it is the only third-party transaction mark; the DCF is the downside cross-check.

The P/BV cross-check is rebuilt. The previous set (ADRO, DSSA, CUAN, ASII) imported the DSSA and CUAN konglo premia into the parent's fundamental value, which the konglo card forbids. The set is now ADRO, ASII and ABMM, the premium-free or discount conglomerates in house coverage, and the median is **0.79x** book rather than the old konglo median [S0]. On the filed post-rights equity of **8,304** and **263,337**m shares that is **Rp25** per share - a cross-check on the same book, not independent evidence, at the config's residual **20%** weight. The P/E leg is removed: FY2025 parent profit of **494** carries the **320** bargain-purchase gain and the **422** remeasurement gain, both one-off, and the parent is loss-making in every forecast year [S12].

VKTR is carried at the book value of the stake, **262**, because it is an uncovered konglo sibling and the group-consistency rule forbids marking it at its listed premium [S12, S25]. The October 2026 rights-issue subscription price values the stake at **2,135**; that is a transaction price, not a fundamental value, and it is the bull's mark step rather than the base [S23, F39].

Two post-balance-sheet items go into the bridge: the rights proceeds of **4,714** and the nine-month loss of **-342**, each once, because both parts are at 31 December 2025 book values [S29]. A holdco discount of **38%** is then applied, at the wide end of the band, for the flags the method card names: offshore control, a minority float, serial issuance, a quasi-reorganization and no dividend [S11, S16]. The primary produces **Rp19** per share.

**What the price implies.** The cost of capital is **12.0%** with a cost of equity of **21.2%** and a levered beta of **2.30** [S0]. A reverse DCF on the holdco discount is not bracketed: at any discount in the method card's band the value is below the price, so the price implies a premium, not a discount [S0]. The price is paying for the toll road's traffic and tariff growth, the EV order book and a manufacturing mark above book; none is sourced well enough to capitalise, and none is in the base.

**The konglo lens.** BNBR is a Bakrie-family holding vehicle with a free float of **28.8%** [S0]. In the 2026 regime the marginal price is set by float and flows, not fundamentals. The price is **2.00x** the fundamental value; the base regime scenario keeps **30%** of the log gap and gives **Rp42**, the bear **Rp31** and the bull **Rp55** [S0]. The premium is a regime variable, never an input.

Mark sensitivity is separate. On CCT, the DCF is below the acquisition mark, so the mark risk is down, not up. The VKTR subscription-price floor of **2,135** against **262** at book is the bull's principal upside. A zero-floor residual or a positive BMI mark would add a little, but no BMI segment accounts are archived. The base uses the sourced book mark.

**Interest and refinancing (high likelihood, high impact).** Operating profit of **596** against interest and financial charges of **815** [S29]. The rights issue cut the debt and cover reaches about breakeven in FY2027E, but the loan is floating-rate and the Bank Nobu facility of **700** matures in November 2026 [S29].

**Pledged shares and the Nobu concentration (high likelihood, medium impact).** The Bank Nobu CCT-acquisition facility is secured by **2,000**m BNBR shares plus BTI, BRMS, ENRG and VKTR shares [S29]. The pledge is documented, contrary to the last draft's "not established", and it is a margin-call and supply risk because the controller's vehicles set the float. Meanwhile **750** of the **954** cash balance sits at the same lender, so the deposit may be compensating in substance [S29].

**Concentration and earnings quality (medium likelihood, high impact).** One asset, one concession, one corridor; the rights proceeds that make book positive sit in the bridge, not in the businesses [S12, S29]. FY2025 is dominated by a one-off gain, FY2024 by gains on loan settlements and asset sales, and the accumulated deficit was eliminated by a quasi-reorganization, so reported profit is not a guide [S11, S12].

**Equity issuance and liquidity (high likelihood, medium impact).** The July issue was struck at **53** a share, raised **4,714**, diluted a non-subscriber by up to **34%**, and the largest holders transferred their entitlement to a standby buyer rather than fund it [S29, S16, F27, F72]; VKTR's own issue diluted non-participating holders by **25.5%** [S25].

**Scenarios.** The probabilities are bear **25%**, base **50%** and bull **25%**. The lens already carries a regime bear, so the business scenarios no longer double-count it. The live methods are the book-value discount (fixed parts) and the P/BV leg (fixed book), so the spread is a discount-and- earnings sensitivity: the bear widens the discount to the top of the band, the bull narrows it, and neither shocks the CCT or VKTR marks. The bear gives **Rp24**, the base **Rp25** and the bull **Rp25** [S0].

**The konglo lens and the regime.** The business scenarios move the fundamental value; a second, independent set of regime scenarios moves the premium. The market pays **2.00x** fundamental, and the lens keeps **30%** of the log gap in the base regime scenario, for a target of **Rp42**; the bear gives **Rp31** and the bull **Rp55** [S0]. The dated events are the minimum free-float step from March 2027, the HSC reviews, and MSCI's Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S0]. Another rights issue, a placement, or a change of control are the other live catalysts [S16].

Signposts that would change the view: a tariff adjustment materially above the scheduled one, interest cover turning positive on the post-rights balance, a funded plan showing the manufacturing and EV businesses earning their cost of capital, or any transaction that upstreams cash to the parent's shareholders.

The ultimate beneficial owners are the three Bakrie brothers; the largest registered holder is at **26.0%** [S11]. The register is not one large holder and a public tail: Fountain City Investment holds **22.2%**, UOB Kay Hian **8.5%**, Eurofa Capital **6.8%**, Levoca Enterprise **5.3%** and PT Biofuel Indo Sumatra **1.3%**, with the public below five per cent each at **30.0%** [S11]. Several large holders are offshore or nominee vehicles, so control is not proportionate to economic ownership.

**Pledged shares.** The last draft said pledges were not established. That was wrong. The short-term-loans note shows the Bank Nobu term loan for the CCT acquisition, still outstanding at **700** at 30 September 2026, secured by **2,000**m BNBR shares plus BTI, BRMS, ENRG and VKTR shares [S29]. The facility is twelve months from 19 November 2025 at **0.1%** and matures in November 2026; a margin call or a refinancing that requires more collateral is a near-term supply and control risk [S29, F100].

**Offshore and structured paper.** The last draft wrongly said short-term investments were nil: the related-party line was nil, but total third-party short-term investments were **1,321** at 31 December 2025 and **1,218** at 30 September 2026 [S29]. The notes describe Bellridge exchangeable bonds and Sherwin and Fortesque placements. Advances for investment are **901**, comprising Fortesque **750** and Mandala Raya Yuwana **151**; the Fortesque funds sit in a designated account managed by Fortesque for BTI, and a Fortesque return was settled through the company's loan to MRY [S29]. These are assets, not losses, but they are offshore, structured and not consolidated operating businesses, and a minority holder cannot mark them.

**Dividend-upstream coverage and look-through leverage.** No cash dividend has been paid and the payout is nil [S6]; the only distributions are to non-controlling interests [S29]. Upstream coverage is nil, not a ratio. Look-through, the debt sits in the parts: the CCT syndicated loan of **9,715** is at the toll-road subsidiary, the BTI facility of **4,362** was at the intermediate holding level, and the remainder sits across the operating subsidiaries [S12, F15, F42]. The lenders hold the share pledge and set the covenants - the maximum debt-to-equity covenant is **6.2x** [S12] - so look-through leverage is worse than the headline.

| Look-through debt | IDR bn | Sits at | Source | |---|---|---|---| | CCT syndicated project loan, FY2025 | 9,715 | toll-road subsidiary | [S12, F15] | | BTI facility (Hartman and Bank Nobu), FY2025 | 4,362 | intermediate holdco | [S19, F42] | | Bank Nobu term loan, 9M26 | 700 | BTI / CCT acquisition | [S29, F84] | | Short-term loans, 9M26 | 2,054 | consolidated operating companies | [S29, F68] | | Long-term loans, 9M26 | 11,275 | consolidated, including CCT | [S29, F69] | | Cash, 9M26 | 954 | consolidated, of which Nobu 750 | [S29, F70, F79] |

The equity history is the governance issue with teeth: a sequence of capital increases and a 2024 quasi-reorganization that eliminated **19,530** of accumulated deficit [S11, S12]. The July 2026 issue continued the pattern: **4,714** of proceeds and **263,337**m shares, most passed through to repay the BTI facility rather than retained [S29, S16]. On ESG, nothing in the record suggests an exposure that changes the valuation [S11].

**The konglo profile.** BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed holding vehicle [S11, S16]. The registry free float is **28.8%**, above the exchange's minimum; the annual report's public-holding figure of **30.0%** is the share held below five per cent each at 31 December 2025, and the gap is definition and date [S0, S11]. BNBR is not on the HSC list as of 22 October 2026, so the HSC index exclusions do not apply; there is no enforcement action or index deletion recorded [S0].

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter: the November 2026 maturity of the Bank Nobu facility that carries the share pledge, the 2026 toll tariff adjustment, the full-year results, the annual meeting, and MSCI's Standalone decision. We watch the syndicated facility's rate at each amendment, traffic and revenue per day against budget, whether VKTR becomes covered, whether the data-centre intention becomes a filed project, and any new pledge or rights issue [S2, S12, S15].
The KPIs we monitor are toll traffic and daily revenue, interest cover, the parent-attributable residual, and the share count - **263,337**m after the rights issue [S29, S0, S12].

bear.narrative: The discount widens to the top of the method card's 20-40% band as the family has to raise equity again to fund a group that still consumes cash; revenue growth is slower than the tariff adjustment implies; and the floating-rate cost of debt is higher after the post-rights structure settles. The red team's F8 is right that the earlier bear discount was outside the method card's band, so the shock is capped at the top of the band, and that the earlier business-bear probability double-counted the konglo lens's own regime bear, so it is cut to match the lens. The holdings marks are fixed by the engine, so the bear moves the discount and the earnings path, not the CCT or VKTR marks; the mark downside is the CCT DCF cross-check in §4, and the dilution risk is stated in the report rather than shocked.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows inside the band; the scheduled 2026 tariff adjustment and the Burangkeng interchange lift toll traffic faster than plan, so revenue growth is higher; and the cost of debt falls as the post-rights structure and the debt repayment settle. The bull's mark upside is shown separately in §4: VKTR re-marked to the Rp200 rights-issue floor against book and CCT left at its acquisition mark, because a house DCF does not support a higher CCT value. The engine's holdings are fixed, so that mark step is not a scenario shock; the scenario table is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is set from the filed nine-month result, not extrapolated from the first half: revenue of 4,125.792 in the nine months to September (F62) with the fourth quarter held at the third quarter's run-rate (nine months plus the third quarter again) implies a full year of about 5,662 and a step of about half on FY2025 [S29, F62]. The step is the full-year consolidation of the CCT toll road, which entered the group only on 28 November 2025, plus the disclosed increases at VKTR, Bakrie Metal Industries and Bakrie Indo Infrastructure [S26, S29]. Because that is a scope change and not a growth trend, the series steps down to a single-digit rate from FY2027E and holds at the house terminal rate thereafter: FY2027E is set at 8%, sourced to the scheduled 2026 CCT tariff adjustment and to traffic already running above the company's own budget (43,911 vehicles a day, F18), not to a forecast-year spike. [S26, S29, S12, S15, F18]

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026, the last actual: gross profit of 1,131.793 on revenue of 4,125.792 is 27.4% of revenue (F63, F62), up from the 25.1% first-half ratio and from FY2025's 19.9%, because FY2025 held only one month of a toll road whose gross margin is far above the manufacturing average; the toll road alone ran at 846 revenue and 694 EBITDA in FY2025 on a standalone basis (F33, F34), so weighting the parts lifts the blended margin [S29, S12, S22]. The third quarter carried a higher margin than the first half; we do not extrapolate that quarter on its own, and the nine-month ratio is the neutral anchor. Held flat after FY2026E: no disclosed contract or tariff schedule justifies a further step. [S29, S12, S22]

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026: total operating expenses of 535.548 on revenue of 4,125.792 are 13.0% of revenue (S29), below the 14.2% first-half ratio and FY2025's 16.8%, which were struck on smaller revenue bases. The nine-month figure is the last actual and already carries the operating-expense mix of a group with the toll road consolidated for the whole period; the third quarter was lighter still, and we do not extrapolate that quarter on its own. The 16.8% audited ratio was Total Beban Usaha of 627.521 on revenue of 3,742.973 (F54, F52, S12). No cost programme is disclosed that would take it lower. [S29, S12]

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026: the company's reported EBITDA of 810.25 less operating profit of 596.245 implies depreciation and amortisation of about 214 on revenue of 4,125.792, i.e. 5.2% of revenue (S26, S29); the fixed-asset depreciation note alone shows 105.313 for the nine months (S29), and the balance is concession and intangible amortisation, which the pack's D&A line omits. The audited FY2025 charge was 171.363 (F6) against the data pack's 22.921, which is the general-and-administrative allocation only. [S29, S26, S12, F6]

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the filed nine-month cash-flow statement: acquisitions of fixed assets of 270.782 on revenue of 4,125.792 are 6.6% of revenue, with the toll rest area, the EV assembly facility and the steel businesses still consuming capital and a further 59.744 spent on toll concession rights (S29); no archived source discloses a taper. [S29]

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 ratio (operating working capital of 1,453.9 on revenue of 3,743.0), which is the last audited figure for a group whose receivables are heavily related-party. [S0]

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set above the FY2025 reported rate of 3.1%, which is distorted by non-taxable bargain-purchase and restructuring gains, and at the low end of the Indonesian corporate range because the group carries tax losses forward after the quasi-reorganization. [S12, S11]

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the filed nine months to September 2026: gross interest on loans and financial charges of 849.451 (the net charge of 814.542 plus interest income of 34.909) against opening debt of 16,739.8 (F15 plus the year-end short- and long-term lines) annualise to about 6.8%, which is the rate this line carries [S29, F66]. That sits in the audited FY2025 band of 3%-10% (Rupiah) and 1%-7% (US dollar), with the toll road's 9,715.21 syndicated facility (F15) the largest single line [S12, F15]. The red team's F5 is right that the forecast must not run the whole horizon on the pre-rights balance: FY2026E interest is struck on the opening 16,739.8 because the rights issue closed at the end of July 2026 and the nine-month filed charge of 814.542 already carries seven months of pre-repayment interest, but the debt is restated to the filed 30 September 2026 balance of 13,328.9 from FY2027E through the negative net-borrowing line below, so the forward interest bill is about 902 rather than 1,202. The rate stays the filed 6.8%; the balance, not the rate, is what changes. [S29, S12, S19, F66, F68, F69]

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Set from the filed nine months: interest income of 34.909 annualised on the opening cash and short-term-investment balance the data pack carries (1,557.8) is about 3.0%, well below the disclosed time-deposit rates of 5.0%-6.25% (F48) because most of the balance is working cash and short-term investments whose income is not all booked as interest. [S29, S12, F48]

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the actual fall in gross debt: the filed balance sheet shows 16,739.8 of interest-bearing debt at 31 December 2025 and 13,328.9 at 30 September 2026 (short-term 2,054.172 plus long-term 11,274.769), a reduction of 3,410.9 after the July 2026 rights issue repaid the BTI facility [S29, F68, F69]. Entering that reduction as negative net borrowing puts the FY2027E opening balance, and therefore the forward interest charge, on the filed post-rights basis, which is what the red team's F5 asks. The 4,713.8 of equity proceeds themselves stay in the valuation bridge: the engine's cash-flow template has no equity-issuance line, so the modelled cash balance turns negative once the repayment is entered - that is a template limitation, not a forecast, and the report quotes the filed 30 September cash of 954.353 and net debt of 12,374.6 instead of the modelled cash line. Later years are held at zero: with no dated new facility in the archive and no dividend, the base case assumes rolling maturities are refinanced flat rather than adding debt, which is a stated financing assumption, not a sourced plan. [S5, S12, S19, S29, F68, F69, F70, F72]

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the filed nine-month other charges of 69.515 plus the foreign-exchange loss of 2.246, net of the 5.166 gain on asset disposals, i.e. about 66.6 for the year (S29 notes 35 and 36), PLUS the filed nine-month net income-tax expense of 47.892 (current tax 62.064 less deferred 14.172) [S29, F90, F91, F92, F85, F86]. The tax must be carried here because the engine charges tax as pos(pbt) x rate and therefore books zero on a consolidated loss, while the company actually paid subsidiary-level current tax in the nine months despite the group loss - the red team's F6 is right. Carrying the 47.892 as a non-operating charge reproduces the filed parent loss instead of implying a profitable fourth quarter; the FY2026E parent loss then lands close to the nine-month actual rather than above it. The note describes the other items as non-operational receipts and payments individually below Rp10bn, so we take the actual once for this year rather than annualising it. Later years are held at zero: FY2025's other income of 401.969 was dominated by the 320.127 one-off gain on the CCT bargain purchase (F14) and no archived source forecasts a further one-off. [S29, S12, F14, F85, F86, F90, F91, F92]

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at 2% against the audited FY2025 ratio of 1.77%, reflecting the large non-controlling interest the consolidation carries (818.494 at 31 December 2025, of which 812.291 is VKTR, F45) and the fact that minorities absorb their share of the group's losses. [S12, F45]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no cash dividend in the period covered by the price history and its stated policy makes any payout conditional on financial condition, positive retained earnings and a shareholders' resolution; the last decision on record was to carry profit to retained earnings, and the group has just raised equity rather than returned it. [S6, S5]

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the July 2026 rights issue at its filed terms: 14 new Series E shares for every 27 old, which is 0.5185185185 of the count in issue at the last filed balance sheet (F8, F9) [S16, S5]. The ratio is the exact filed one and reconciles the forecast share vector to the pro-forma total of 263,336.672m in F8; nothing is assumed after that.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for an Indonesian rupiah reporter: long-run nominal GDP, no company-specific claim. [S0]

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 38%, at the wide end of the 20-40% band the method card says a family holding company's discount persists in, not at the mid-band 33% the first draft used. The red team's C9 is right that 33% had no name-specific anchor; the anchor now used is the set of flags the card says keep a discount wide, every one of which this name carries: a controlling family whose stakes sit behind British Virgin Islands vehicles (F32), a public float of 29.98% (F31), serial equity issuance that has repeatedly reset the share count and most recently struck a rights issue at Rp53, a quasi-reorganization that eliminated 19,530 of accumulated deficit in 2024 (F30), and a dividend record of nil, so cash does not reach the parent's shareholders. The card's dividend-upstream law says a holdco that neither distributes nor covers its own costs deserves the widest discount in its range, which is what 38% is. The discount is applied and not narrowed: the method card makes the discount the base rate, not the opportunity, and this file has no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (no buyback, tender, asset sale, sub-IPO, simplification or control change is dated in the record), so the discount is not credited with narrowing. The 0.38 is a chosen discount level, not the archetype's probability of narrowing: the 'rate' field in data/base_rates.yaml is that success probability and is not read as the discount itself. BNBR's own five-year discount history cannot be computed here - no house sum-of-the-parts exists before this file - so the band plus the flags is the best available anchor. [S11, F30, F31, F32, S16]

challenges.challenge: The primary 80%-weight "SOTP" is circular. fund record entries CCT at F44 4,101.321, VKTR at F58 262.168 and "all other businesses" at -510.32, but that last line is defined as parent equity F10 3,853.170 less the two marks (4,101.321 + 262.168 - 510.319 = 3,853.170). The sum is therefore book equity by construction; the bridge (rights +4,713.843, loss -341.851) takes it to 8,225.16, which is the filed 30 September 2026 parent equity of 8,303.696 less the 78.53 other-equity movement. Re-marking CCT or VKTR only moves the residual, never the total, so the SOTP per share (19) is simply 0.62 x book equity per share. §4's claims that "the marks are the constraint" (not the cost of capital) and that a "sum of the parts" is below the price are therefore false as written. No holdco opex is capitalised either, contrary to VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §1.
challenges.answer: The residual is the accounting plug and the SOTP total equals book equity by construction; re-marking CCT or VKTR only moves the residual. We relabel the primary a book-value discount in the summary, thesis and §4, and stop claiming the marks are the constraint. We built the CCT concession DCF the challenge asks for: on CCT standalone revenue/EBITDA/operating cash flow (846/694/684), the net concession right (15,018.572), the syndicated debt (9,715.21) and life to 2061, a 10%-12% project cost of capital gives an equity value at or below zero, so the acquisition mark is generous, not conservative. A bottom-up mark of the non-CCT/non-VKTR businesses cannot be sourced (revenue only, no segment EBITDA/EBIT); holdco opex is not separately capitalised because no parent-only P&L is archived, and we state that. Rating re-opened: the fundamental is now about 25, the target about 42, TR +1.5%, HOLD; the HOLD is a konglo-lens carry, not a fundamental margin.

challenges.challenge: The P/BV leg (56/share) carries 20% of the blend even though §4 itself calls it "a loose upper reference, not independent evidence". Its 1.79x peer median is struck on ADRO 0.85x, ASII 0.73x, DSSA 2.84x and CUAN 6.98x (cov_publish comps), i.e. two konglo names whose listed premia the konglo card says must be excluded from a parent's fundamental value. With the 80% leg at 0.62x book, the P/BV leg supplies 11.29 of the 26.78 blend, or 42% of the fundamental value in practice. On the SOTP leg alone the 12-month fundamental is ~23.5 and the lens target ~40, below the Rp41 price, i.e. SELL rather than HOLD.
challenges.answer: Accepted the peer-set correction: DSSA and CUAN are konglo:true names and their listed premia are regime variables, so they are removed from the P/BV set under VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §4. The leg is rebuilt on ADRO, ASII and ABMM at a 0.79x median rather than 1.79x; the P/BV value falls from 56.4 to 24.8 per share and supplies about a quarter of the blend, not 42%. The rating conclusion is rebutted on the house bands: on the SOTP leg alone the lens target is about 39.6, a TR of about -3.4%, which is inside the HOLD band (-10% to +10%), not SELL. With the corrected P/BV cross-check the target is about 41.6 and TR about +1.5%, still HOLD. The call is a narrow lens carry, and the report says so.

challenges.challenge: §6 says pledges "are not quantified in the record and we report that as not established". The record does quantify them: S29 Note 19 (page 83) shows the Bank Nobu term loan for the CCT acquisition, still outstanding at Rp700.025bn at 30 September 2026, is secured by 2,000,000,000 BNBR shares, 2,100 BTI shares, 49,350,889 BRMS shares, 85,776,990 ENRG shares and 1,022,500,000 VKTR shares. VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §3 requires pledged shares to be sourced; treating a documented share pledge as "not established" understates the margin-call and supply risk in a stock where the controller's vehicles set the float.
challenges.answer: The pledge is documented in S29 Note 19 p.83: the Bank Nobu CCT-acquisition term loan (700.025 outstanding at 30 September 2026, 7.00%, twelve months from 19 November 2025) is secured by 2,000,000,000 BNBR shares plus BTI, BRMS, ENRG and VKTR shares. The 'not established' wording is deleted; §6 carries the facility, the pledged BNBR shares, the lender and the November 2026 maturity, and §5 adds the margin-call and near-term supply risk to the bear. We note the pledged shares are BNBR shares held by BTI, not controller vehicles, so the supply risk is real but smaller than a controller pledge of the same size.

challenges.challenge: The governance section omits the offshore and structured asset side, and its wording misleads. §6 says "the short-term-investment balance itself was nil at 31 December 2025": that is true only of the related-party line (S12 p.12), while total short-term investments were Rp1,321.168bn at 31 December 2025 and Rp1,217.825bn at 30 September 2026 (S29 p.5, Note 6). Of the Sept-2026 balance, Bellridge Holdings exchangeable bonds are Rp652.688bn (11% coupon, exchangeable into instruments of Bellridge or its affiliates), Sherwin Investment (Marshall Islands) Rp404.060bn and Fortesque funds Rp58.489bn. Separately, "advances for investment" are Rp901.020bn (Fortesque Rp750.000bn, PT Mandala Raya Yuwana Rp151.020bn, S29 Note 18), and a Rp91.5bn Fortesque return was settled through the Company's loan to MRY. Together ~Rp2.1tn, or ~8% of total assets, sits in opaque offshore structures that §6 does not mention.
challenges.answer: The nil-statement was wrong: it described the related-party line only. Total third-party short-term investments were 1,321.168 at 31 December 2025 and 1,217.825 at 30 September 2026 (S29 p.5/Note 6), including Bellridge exchangeable bonds and Sherwin/Fortesque placements; advances for investment are 901.020 (Fortesque 750.000, MRY 151.020; Note 18). §6 now separates related-party from third-party, explains the Fortesque/MRY circularity (a Fortesque return settled through the company's loan to MRY), and treats them as offshore, structured assets a minority cannot mark.

challenges.challenge: Interest is struck on pre-rights opening debt of 16,739.8 at 6.77% (FY2026E 1,133.9, FY2027E 1,201.6), although the filed 30 September balance is gross debt of 13,328.9 (2,054.2 short-term + 11,274.8 long-term) against cash of 954.4, net debt 12,374.6. At the same rate the post-rights run-rate is ~902, so the model overstates annual interest by roughly 230-300 and turns "operating profit does not cover interest in any year" into a pre-issue artefact: FY2027E EBIT of 883.6 against ~902 post-rights is a ~1.0x cover that a tariff step flips positive. §3 discloses the engine limitation but does not quantify it.
challenges.answer: Forecast debt is restated to the filed post-rights balance: net borrowing FY2026E is -3,410.9 (gross debt 16,739.8 at 31 December 2025 to 13,328.9 at 30 September 2026), so FY2027E opening debt is 13,328.9 and interest falls to about 902.9 from 1,201.6, at the filed 6.77% rate. On that basis FY2027E EBIT of 883.6 covers interest about once and cover is above one from FY2028E; the 'never covers' claim is corrected. The equity proceeds stay in the valuation bridge; the modelled cash line is negative because the engine has no equity-issuance line, and the report tells the reader to use the filed cash and debt.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E np_parent is -328.9 but the nine-month actual is already -341.9, so the model implies a profitable fourth quarter (+12.9) although §3 says Q4 is "carried ... against the same interest bill". The cause is the tax line: the engine applies zero tax to a full-year loss (pos(pbt) x rate), removing the Rp47.892bn current tax actually booked in the 9M LK (S29 p.8, mostly subsidiary-level current tax), while 9M NCI was +9.067. On the filed tax basis the full-year loss is closer to -377.
challenges.answer: The nine-month income tax charge is real (current 62.064 less deferred 14.172 = 47.892 net) even though the consolidated result is a loss, because it is booked at profitable subsidiaries; the engine taxes only a positive consolidated pre-tax profit and would remove it. We carry the 47.892 as a non-operating charge in FY2026E so the forecast reproduces the filed nine months. FY2026E np_parent is now -375.85 against the 9M actual -341.85, i.e. a loss-making Q4, not a profitable one.

challenges.challenge: The base case capitalises none of the sourced upside. CCT is kept at its November 2025 acquisition value although traffic is 3.25% above RKAP and revenue per day 3.02% above (S15 p.14), a 2026 tariff increase is scheduled, and the Q3 gross margin is ~31.4% against 27.4% for the nine months; the report itself says a house DCF would show it "worth more". VKTR is marked at book 262.2 although the October 2026 rights price of Rp200/share values the stake at 2,135.4 (F57) and the post-rights net-asset accretion (~Rp480bn) is noted in post_bs_review but never bridged. The zero-floor and positive BMI mark are described but not quantified.
challenges.answer: We built the transparent concession DCF the challenge asks for, with stated inputs: CCT revenue 846, EBITDA 694 and operating cash flow 684 (FY2025), a 2,500/day revenue run-rate, the net concession right of 15,018.572 over the remaining life to 2061, and project debt of 9,715.21. The result rebuts the premise that a house DCF would be worth more: at a 10%-12% project cost of capital the PV of the road's cash flow does not cover the debt, so the equity is at or below zero and the acquisition mark of 4,101.321 is generous. The DCF is therefore a downside cross-check, not a capitalised mark, and the bull does not claim a higher CCT mark; the sourced VKTR floor is the bull's mark step. The report no longer asserts a house DCF would show CCT worth more.

challenges.challenge: The scenario architecture is decorative. Of the three mirrored shocks (holdco discount +/-10pp, revenue growth +/-3pp, cost of debt +/-1.5pp), only the discount reaches either live method, because the SOTP parts and the P/BV equity are fixed; the 29/32/35 spread is therefore a discount-only sensitivity and neither the CCT nor the VKTR mark is ever shocked. The bear adds 10pp to a 38% discount, giving 48%, which is outside VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT's 20-40% band, yet the bear narrative calls it "the top of the band". The 35% business-bear probability is also set from the konglo regime that the lens already carries with its own 25% regime-bear, double-counting the regime.
challenges.answer: The bear discount is capped at the top of the 20-40% band (38% base +2pp = 40%) instead of 48%, and the business probabilities are re-weighted to bear 25 / base 50 / bull 25 to match the konglo lens's own regime probabilities and remove the double-count. The report states plainly that the live methods carry fixed parts and fixed book, so the spread is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity, not a mark sensitivity; the CCT DCF and VKTR floor are shown separately in §4 with the mark risk direction. The 40% cap and the 25% bear are sourced to the method card and the lens, not to a forecast.

challenges.challenge: The liquidity picture omits a counterparty concentration that changes the net-debt reading. At 30 September 2026, Rp750.004bn of the Rp954.353bn cash balance (79%) is held at PT Bank Nationalnobu (S29 Note 5 p.53), the same bank that carries the Rp700.025bn CCT-acquisition term loan (Note 19 p.82). §3 and §6 present "cash of 954" and a "materially lighter balance" as free liquidity and compute net debt on gross cash.
challenges.answer: At 30 September 2026, 750.004 of the 954.353 cash balance sits at PT Bank Nationalnobu, the lender on the 700.025 CCT-acquisition facility; the deposit is not presented as restricted but the counterparty is the same one that holds the share pledge, so the economic netting is unclear. §5 and §6 disclose the concentration and present available liquidity as the non-Nobu balance; the filed net debt is the three balance-sheet lines, not the modelled cash line.

challenges.challenge: The share register is only half reported. §6 gives Port Fraser International 26.01% and the public below 5% at 29.98%, but the annual report lists five further >5% holders: Fountain City Investment 22.17%, UOB Kay Hian 8.47%, Eurofa Capital 6.76%, Levoca Enterprise 5.32% and PT Biofuel Indo Sumatra 1.29% (S11 p.11), i.e. 70.0% in six names, several of them offshore/nominee vehicles. VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §3 requires shareholders above 5% and the affiliates behind the float; without them the report's claim that control is "not proportionate to economic ownership" cannot be tested.
challenges.answer: The full >5% register is now reported: Fountain City 22.17%, UOB Kay Hian 8.47%, Eurofa 6.76%, Levoca 5.32%, plus the ultimate parent PT Biofuel Indo Sumatra 1.29% and Port Fraser 26.01%, with the public below 5% at 29.98% (S11 p.11). Several holders are offshore/nominee vehicles; we identify them as such and stop claiming the register is one large holder and a public tail. The registry free float of 28.76% is a different definition and date from the 29.98% public figure, and §6 says so.

challenges.challenge: The CCT mark is internally inconsistent with its own label. The holdings entry is titled "CCT, 99.99% via Bakrie Toll Indonesia" but is valued at F44 4,101.321, which is 4,317.180 less the Rp215.859 "NCI portion" (i.e. 95%); the FY2025 subsidiary list shows 99.99% at 31 December 2025 and the 9M list shows 98.51%/99.99% (S12 p.25; S29 p.20), while S18 describes a move from 10% to 100%. The mark is not reconciled to the ownership. Because the residual is a plug, the error does not move the SOTP total, which is itself the F1 problem.
challenges.answer: The holding label is corrected: CCT is 99.99% legally via Bakrie Toll Indonesia, but the audited acquisition NCI line implies a lower effective interest, which is the 4,101.321 mark. §1 and §4 state the unreconciled difference and say we use the filed mark rather than gross up, so the mark is if anything slightly low on ownership, not high.

challenges.challenge: §3 and the summary say the parent lost Rp342 "because interest and financial charges of 815 ... exceeded operating profit of 596". The arithmetic gap is Rp123bn: other charges -69.515, FX -2.246, disposal +5.166, tax -47.892 and NCI +9.067 (S29 pp.8-9). The interest-cover point survives, but the causal attribution as written is incomplete and understates the non-interest losses.
challenges.answer: The §3 sentence now gives the full walk from operating profit to the parent loss: operating profit 596.245 plus a 5.166 disposal gain less a 2.246 FX loss, 814.542 of interest and 69.515 of other charges gives a pre-tax loss of 284.892; the 47.892 net tax charge and the 9.067 NCI credit take it to the parent loss of 341.851. The interest-cover point survives, and the non-interest losses are no longer omitted.

challenges.challenge: The update runs about 6,460 prose words against the constitution's update_words band of 500-3,500 (WARN), and the excess is largely repetition of the same bear points across §1, §3, §5 and §6. Length is not evidence, and the repetition makes the file read more bearish than the HOLD with a 7.8% expected return supports.
challenges.answer: The report is cut to 3,500 prose words from about 6,460, inside the update band, and the repeated bear points across §1, §3, §5 and §6 are removed. The remaining length is the evidence the 17 challenges require: the F1 relabel, the CCT DCF cross-check, the pledge/register/offshore-paper corrections and the earnings-quality walk.

challenges.challenge: The D&A basis misdescribes the number. da_pct is derived as EBITDA 810.25 less EBIT 596.245 = 214.0 (5.19%), and the basis calls the balance over the Rp105.313 fixed depreciation "concession and intangible amortisation"; but the 9M LK separately discloses Rp329.2bn of toll-concession amortisation charged to cost of revenues (S29 p.75). The 214.0 add-back is therefore not total D&A and the company's "EBITDA" evidently excludes the concession amortisation.
challenges.answer: The EBITDA convention is now defined: the company-reported EBITDA of 810.25 (9M) is operating profit 596.245 plus a 214.0 add-back that excludes the 329.2 amortisation of the toll-road concession charged to cost of revenues (S29 p.75). The model follows the company convention; if the concession amortisation is added back too, EBITDA is higher and leverage lower. §3 states the convention, reconciles the two numbers and no longer describes the 214.0 as total D&A.

challenges.challenge: VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §3 requires §4 to show what the price implies (reverse DCF); the report instead asserts that "the price already assumes that all three go right" from the fact that the price exceeds a book-based SOTP. That gap is equally consistent with the excluded VKTR market premium (Rp7.2tn at the Rp675 theoretical ex-rights price) or with an unmodelled CCT DCF, so the claim is not evidenced.
challenges.answer: §4 now states what the price implies: the price is 2.00x the probability-weighted fundamental value, the cost of capital is 12.0% (COE 21.2%, levered beta 2.30), and a reverse DCF on the holdco discount is not bracketed because at any discount in the method card's band the value is below the price, so the price implies a premium, not a discount. The report no longer asserts 'the price already assumes all three go right' without evidence; it says the price is paying for traffic/tariff growth, the EV order book and a manufacturing mark above book, none sourced well enough to capitalise.

challenges.challenge: EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS §3 gates investability on IDX board/notation status, and the report never states whether BNBR is on the special-monitoring board (papan pemantauan khusus) or carries a notation letter; it also presents no accruals or cash-conversion line. For the record, the 9M accruals ratio is about -1.7% (NI -332.8 less CFO 80.3 on average assets ~24.6tn), which is not a manipulation flag but should be shown.
challenges.answer: The nine-month accruals ratio is added to §3 (net income less operating cash flow, over average total assets; datapoint 67, 88, 87 and 101) and is negative, so it is not a manipulation flag. On the IDX board/notation status, no direct exchange notice is archived: the data pack's investability screen returns the board as normal, and BNBR is absent from the 28 September 2026 list of names removed from the special-monitoring board (S30). We report the absence of a special-board finding rather than assert a clean bill.

challenges.challenge: §4 own mark-sensitivity paragraph says the VKTR floor (2,135.4 vs 262.2 book) and a CCT house value would lift the SOTP materially and that these are the untested levers, and they all point one way - up, but no number, probability or scenario uses them: the bull explicitly does not re-mark CCT or VKTR. At the VKTR Rp200 floor alone the stake is worth 1,873.2bn more, about Rp7.1/share before the discount, and the Q3 CCT margin and 2026 tariff step are similarly uncapitalised. A base case may decline to capitalise unsourced marks, but a bull scenario that ignores the only two sourced higher marks is not a bull.
challenges.answer: The bull now carries the sourced higher marks: VKTR re-marked to the October 2026 subscription-price floor (2,135.369 against 262.168 at book) is its principal upside, and the report shows the sensitivity in §4. CCT is not re-marked higher because the house DCF is below the acquisition mark, not above it; the acquisition mark is already generous. At the VKTR floor alone the stake is worth about 1,873 more, a little over 7 per share before the discount, which lifts the bull but does not close the gap to the price. The scenario table remains a discount sensitivity because the engine's holdings are fixed; the report says the mark step is not in the shocks.

missing_bull_case.note: The sourced CCT ramp (traffic 3.25% above RKAP, 2026 tariff increase, Q3 gross margin ~31.4% vs 27.4% 9M), the VKTR Rp200 subscription floor (2,135.4 vs 262.2 book) and the post-rights VKTR book accretion are all named but never quantified; §4 says a house DCF would value CCT above the acquisition mark yet does not build one (F7).

missing_bear_case.note: Pledged shares (S29 Note 19 p.83), the ~Rp2.1tn offshore/structured investments and Fortesque/MRY advances (S29 Notes 6 and 18), the 79% of cash held at Bank Nobu against a Nobu loan, and the six >5% shareholders (S11 p.11) are absent, and the bear never shocks the CCT or VKTR marks (F3, F4, F9, F10, F8).

assumption_realism.note: The three drivers that move value are not consistent with the last actual: interest is struck on pre-rights debt of 16,739.8 against the filed 13,328.9, the FY tax line is zero against the 9M Rp47.9bn current-tax charge, and the FY2026E parent loss is smaller than the 9M actual, implying a profitable Q4 (F5, F6).

evidence_and_citations.note: Load-bearing claims are contradicted by the archived filing: pledges are quantified (p.83), total short-term investments are Rp1,321bn at Dec-2025, not nil (p.5), the CCT holding label (99.99%) is unreconciled with the 95% value, and the D&A composition is misdescribed (F3, F4, F11, F14).

valuation_method_fit.note: The 80% "SOTP" is circular: the residual is the accounting plug, so the SOTP equals book equity and the CCT/VKTR marks cancel. The 20% P/BV leg imports konglo premia and is the difference between HOLD and SELL; CCT is never valued on its own concession and holdco opex is not capitalised (F1, F2, F7, F15).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is more bearish than the HOLD with a 7.8% expected return supports; "the price already assumes that all three go right" is asserted without a reverse DCF, the update is ~6,460 words against a 3,500 band, and the business-scenario probabilities double-count the konglo regime (F8, F13, F15).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: COE 21.2% / WACC 12.0% and the balance-of-payments / CAUTIOUS macro tilt are read consistently, and the Rupiah cost of debt is the LK's nine-month effective rate; the remaining inconsistency is the peer multiple source, filed under valuation_method_fit (F2).

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked conservatism that moves the value: a 38% discount on a book-based sum with no five-year history anchor, a 48% bear discount outside the 20-40% band, pre-rights interest, VKTR at book versus a Rp200 floor, and no credit for the Q3 margin. Only the zero tax line runs optimistic (F5, F7, F8, F6).

calibration.note: FY+1 does not reproduce the last actual: FY2026E parent loss of -329 against the filed 9M loss of -342 implies a profitable fourth quarter, driven by the engine's zero tax on a full-year loss; the BLOCK flags themselves are sourced and justified (F6).

signoff.notes: APPROVED — HOLD, target Rp42, TR +1.5%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish. F1 (FATAL) is answered on substance: the 80% "SOTP" is relabelled a book-value discount because the residual is the accounting plug and CCT/VKTR re-marks only move it; a concession DCF of CCT is shown as a downside cross-check; and the rating was re-opened. F2-F10 and F17 (MATERIAL) are answered: the P/BV peer set is cleansed of the DSSA/CUAN konglo premia to ADRO/ASII/ABMM at 0.79x (the same VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §4 rule), pledges, offshore paper, the >5% register, the Nobu cash concentration and the post-rights debt are all sourced, and the P/E leg is dropped because there is no maintainable parent earnings. Lint PASS (WARN: primary + one cross-check, reasoned). KONGLO-GROUP READ: BNBR is Bakrie; the only covered sibling is VKTR and it is carried at book, not at its listed premium, so the group-consistency rule is met. BATCH BIAS: not a single systematic tilt. BNBR's target is above price only because the konglo lens keeps 1.677x of a 2.00x premium on a fundamental (Rp25) that is 39% BELOW the Rp41 price — the opposite underlying edge to TOBA's SOTP≈price, so the two calls are independent; the shared COE (21.2% vs 20.3%) is the engine's beta-derived input, and both holdco discounts are conservative. Residual non-blocking QC FIX items, none affecting HOLD/Rp42, to clean at the next update: Q1 the base regime scenario is Rp40, not Rp42 (Rp42 is the probability-weighted lens target) and the prose still prints 42 as the base; Q3 state the CCT DCF's exact project rate, growth path, PV and equity — the prose's "at or below zero" is stronger than the arithmetic supports ("below the 4,101 acquisition mark" holds at 9-12%); Q2 state the residual construction once, since the VKTR floor cannot be both "only moves the residual" and additive bull upside; Q4 footnote or override the FY2026E net-debt row (engine 16,394 vs filed 12,375). Contamination: none — no consensus, broker target or third-party estimate was used or found.

bias.note: HOLD is carried by the konglo lens, not a directional fundamental view: 12-month fundamental Rp24.8 against a Rp41 price, disclosed. Errors run both ways and do not move the rating - minor conservatism (the 0.79x P/BV median is a total-equity multiple applied to parent equity; VKTR at book below the Rp200 floor; the CCT DCF at the top of a 10-12% range) against minor optimism (CCT kept at its acquisition mark although the DCF is below it). No unsourced base-case driver departs from the last actual: FY2026E gross margin, opex and D&A are the filed 9M ratios; the only calibration gap is the sourced CCT consolidation scope change (S18, S22, S29).

findings.finding: §4 and §5 say "the base regime scenario keeps 30% of the log gap and gives Rp42". The engine's base regime scenario gives Rp40.35 (bear 30.56, bull 55.17); Rp42 (41.61) is the probability-weighted lens target, not the base scenario. The header target construction "20 x (1+COE) ... = base 25" likewise reads as 25 x (1 - 0%) = 42 and only reconciles through the 1.677 premium. The judge raised the same point (NOTE).

Thesis, summary and §4 say "the total is book equity by construction" and "re-marking CCT or VKTR only moves the residual", but §4 presents the VKTR Rp200 subscription floor (2,135 against 262 book, about Rp7/share before the discount) as "the bull's principal upside" and a zero-floor residual as additive. Under a plug definition no re-mark can lift the total; under a fixed-other-businesses definition the VKTR floor does lift it. The report uses both readings. The base, target and rating do not depend on it.

The CCT concession DCF is not reproducible: the report and assumptions give only a "10%-12% project cost of capital" with no exact rate, cash-flow growth/ramp or PV/equity figure. On the sourced FY2025 OCF of 684 over the ~35-year concession, flat OCF gives a PV near 6.6tn at 10% (equity about -3.1tn), but 4% growth gives near 9.8tn (equity about zero) and at 9% with growth the equity is about +1.3tn. "At or below zero" is therefore not established across the stated range, though "below the 4,101 acquisition mark" holds at 9-12%.

The fin_summary net-debt row shows FY2026E 16,394 against the filed 30 September 2026 net debt of 12,375 (13,328.9 debt less 954.4 cash, S29), because the engine has no equity-issuance cash line. §3 discloses the artefact, so it is not a BLOCK, but the table still prints the wrong figure and the company's filed 2025 total interest-bearing borrowings note reads 17,023.4, not the 16,739.8 opening balance used.

The 0.79x peer median is market cap / total equity (including NCI) for ADRO, ASII and ABMM, but it is applied to BNBR's parent equity (F59 8,303.696). Mixing bases understates the P/BV leg by about 7-8% (roughly Rp2.4/share, roughly Rp0.5/share after the 20% weight). Immaterial to HOLD.

The bear/base/bull shocks are mirrored (±2pp holdco discount, ±3pp revenue growth, ±1.5pp cost of debt) and the 25/50/25 probabilities put base at 50% - compliant. But only the discount reaches either live method (SOTP = book x discount; P/BV = book x multiple): the revenue and cost-of-debt shocks do not move value, so the 24/25/25 spread is discount-only and the prose's "discount-and-earnings sensitivity" overstates what the earnings shocks do. The judge raised the tight-range point.

§4 says the bridge "takes the total to filed parent equity", but the parts plus the two bridge items sum to 8,225.2; the 78.53 other equity-components movement (which the assumptions note) is not in the bridge, while the P/BV leg uses 8,303.7. A ~1% basis gap between the two live legs, immaterial.

On the rounded display (42/41)-1 = 2.4%, not the printed 1.5%; the engine's unrounded 41.61/41.0 gives 1.49%, so 1.5% is right on exact inputs but the rounded header invites the 2.4% read. The judge raised the same point (NOTE).

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +11.9pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A economic margin is not comparable to FY2026E because it contains only one month of the toll road, consolidated from 28 November 2025 [S18, F12]: the audited year shows operating expenses of 627.521 on revenue of 3,742.973, i.e. 16.8% of revenue, and the toll road alone ran at 846 revenue and 694 EBITDA in FY2025 (F33, F34) at a margin far above the manufacturing average [S12, S22]. The FY2026E ratios are anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026, which already carry the toll road for the full period: revenue of 4,125.792 with gross profit of 1,131.793 (27.4%), operating expenses of 535.548 (13.0%), operating profit of 596.245 and reported EBITDA of 810.25 [S29, S26, F62, F63, F64, F65]. On the restated base FY2025A EBITDA margin is 7.7% against a 19.6% FY2026E, a +11.9pp step that is scope and mix, not margin expansion, and the report says so.

flags.message: ebit FY2025A restated at 11.09x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack's FY2025A operating profit of 10.536 is the general-and-administrative stub only: the audited consolidated statement of profit or loss shows LABA USAHA (operating profit) of 116.863 after Total Beban Usaha operating expenses of 627.521 [S12, F52, F54]. Restating ebit and opex to the filing reconciles the statement - gross profit 744.384 less opex 627.521 equals 116.863 - and corrects the calibration base; the pack's allocation is the wrong figure, not the filing.

flags.message: balance-sheet equity restated at 2.24x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The balance-sheet equity used by the P/BV leg is restated to the filed 8,303.696 of parent equity at 30 September 2026 (F59, S29) against the data pack's 3,710.09, a 2.24x step. The pack's figure is the 30 June 2026 balance sheet struck before the end-July 2026 rights issue and before the nine-month result; the filing shows Rp4,713.8bn of proceeds from the issuance of capital stock (F72) and a nine-month parent-attributable loss of Rp341.9bn (F67), and the share count is 263.34bn (F71, S29). Dividing pre-rights equity by post-rights shares is the base mismatch the red team's C3 identified, so the equity metric is restated to the filed post-rights balance and not the other way round. The pack's field is stale, not wrong for its date.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The P/E leg is removed because it has no maintainable earnings to capitalise: FY2025 reported parent profit of 493.852 carries the 320.127 bargain-purchase gain (F14) and the 422.375 gain on remeasurement of the previously held equity interest (F56), both non-recurring and struck on the November 2025 acquisition [S12 p.15], and the parent is loss-making in every forecast year. Normalising those out leaves a negative figure, so the leg is inapplicable; the weight moves to the SOTP (0.8) and the P/BV cross-check (0.2). The red team's F1 is accepted: the SOTP leg is a book-value discount, not an independent sum of the parts, so the report labels it that way and does not treat the P/BV leg as independent confirmation. The red team's F2 is also accepted on the peer set: DSSA and CUAN were removed because their 2.8x and 6.8x P/BV are konglo regime premia (VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4), and the leg is rebuilt on the premium-free ADRO, ASII and ABMM (about 0.79x median) rather than 1.79x. [S11, S12, F14]

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 2.00x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 30% of the log gap in 12 months (no regime flags); target 42 vs fundamental 12-month value 25 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens reading is expected for a konglo whose float is thin: the market pays about 2.0x our probability-weighted fundamental value of about 20 and the base regime scenario keeps 30% of that log gap over 12 months, giving a target near 42 against the 12-month fundamental value of about 25 [S0, S11]. The premium is a regime variable, not a valuation input - the fundamental value is our own and the third-quarter filing changed only the operating forecast and the book equity, not the marks - and the report states plainly in §4 and §5 that the small expected return is this lens carry rather than discount narrowing, which is why the call is HOLD. The prior draft's P/BV leg overstated the fundamental by using konglo-premium peers; with the premium-free set the fundamental falls to about 20 and the lens carries a target of about 42, so the call is a narrow HOLD with no fundamental cushion. The konglo profile is in §6.
